Two deals are late-stage: a healthcare deployment (~$600k ACV) where Redwood Dedicated + private deployment is favored for data residency, and a fintech POC (~$250k) leaning hosted with strict audit logs. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood Partner Mgr), Oliver Reese (Borealis Channel Lead), Maya Lin (Borealis VP Partnerships), Samir Khanna (Borealis Solutions Architect)
Links shared: pipeline spreadsheet https://redwood.app/pipeline/borealis-q4, security docs https://redwood.app/security, enablement deck (deck link)

00:00 Sasha: Alright, hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick check-in on the co-sell pipeline, 45 minutes on the calendar. Sasha here, AE on the account.
00:23 Oliver: Hey Sasha, thanks. We got a couple of folks on, Maya and Samir are on my side, so appreciate it.
00:30 Diego: hey hi, this is Diego from Redwood SE, I'll cover tech asks and benchmarks, quick intro.
00:45 Maya: quick note, we're trying to focus the reps on three priority deals for Q4, trying to keep it tight.
01:10 Sasha: Great, that's the plan. I'll share the spreadsheet after this, but first can we run through the active opps — I have six listed, want to confirm your view.
01:35 Oliver: yes six sounds right. Quick summary: health system (late stage), large retailer (mid), fintech POC (late), telco pilot (early), logistics POC (mid), and a government RFP (early).
02:05 Sasha: Perfect. The two late-stage ones — can we start with the health system? That one you said was leaning to private deployment because of residency and HIPA — HIPAA sorry.
02:25 Samir: yeah HIPAA, our security team is strict. For the health deal they want VPC and dedicated capacity. They asked about KMS integration and audit logs.
02:40 Diego: we can do KMS/HSM integrations, and we have audit log exports. Diego: small caveat, for very strict residency they want on-prem or air-gapped, we can talk through that path, it's a bit longer.
03:05 Maya: timeframe on on-prem is concern — client wants Q1 go-live, so we prefer Redwood Dedicated in their cloud region if possible.
03:22 Sasha: Understood. For Redwood Dedicated we can propose reserved capacity and SLA, and we can also provide SOC 2/ISO artifacts. I'll attach the security pack.
03:45 Oliver: that helps. Do you have numbers on latency/cost tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated? The CFO will ask.
04:02 Diego: yes, we ran benchmarks — typical delta is 10-30% lower per-token cost on Dedicated when you amortize reserved capacity for steady throughput; latency is slightly better for hosted in bursty loads but Dedicated gives predictable p99 under heavy sustained loads. I'll share the benchmark slides.
04:28 Samir: can you run a benchmark using our sample workload? We have a long-context clinical summarization prompt — that kills performance on some runtimes.
04:40 Diego: absolutely, schedule the benchmark and send the sample prompts, we'll do a run on both hosted and dedicated variants and give a cost/latency table.
04:55 Maya: good. Next: fintech POC — we need fast time-to-value and tight audit trails. That one could be hosted if you provide the right EDP/PII handling.
05:12 Sasha: ok we can propose hosted with strict retention policies and encryption at rest + customer-managed keys if needed.
05:28 Oliver: competitor question — some of our partners push OpenAI or Anthropic, how do you position Redwood?
05:38 Sasha: we position Redwood as production-first with cost controls and unified runtime across private/dedicated/hosted. We also emphasize model catalog and predictable SLOs; plus dev experience for quick integration.
05:58 Maya: pricing will be key, the field asks comparative per-token rates.
06:10 Diego: we'll provide a unit economics sheet comparing typical per-token costs and expected savings from batching and KV cache for prefix workloads.
06:30 Oliver: Great. Any blockers on the retail deal? They asked about multi-region routing and regional data residency.
06:45 Diego: multi-region is supported via smart routing, we can set policy to prefer region-local inference and fallback. Some misconfiguration risk but we'll help with runbooks.
07:05 Samir: for the government RFP, they asked about on-prem options and FedRAMP. Do you have a FedRAMP plan?
07:20 Sasha: we don't currently have FedRAMP at GA, but we can support on-prem private deployments and work with partners for gov clouds. We should be transparent on that in the RFP response.
07:40 Maya: ok noted.
07:55 Sasha: quick pause — I want to call out two deals we should prioritize for co-sell enablement: health system (600k ACV) and fintech POC (250k). If Borealis can get intro to procurement and architecture that's big.
08:20 Oliver: we can do the procurement intros once we have the security pack and pilot plan.
08:35 Diego: on pilot plan, tech ask: what's the expected seq length and throughput? That'll drive kernel selection and cost.
08:50 Samir: for the health care workload, avg prompt 2.5k tokens, peaks 8k with long KV caches for patient history. For fintech it's shorter, 1k tokens.
09:10 Diego: good that's useful. We'll configure Dedicated with quantization profiles for long context and measure memory footprint.
09:25 Sasha: action: Diego will run cost/latency benchmarks for those two profiles and share by next week.
09:40 Maya: on enablement, the field wants a one-pager and a joint case study template. We can co-brand something.
09:55 Priya: Priya here — Redwood can provide a joint one-pager and a 30-min enablement session for Borealis sellers. I'll put together slides and a script.
10:10 Oliver: ideal. Sales ops wants an intro email template as well.
10:25 Priya: we'll include an email template in the enablement pack.
10:40 Sasha: switching to pipeline specifics: I have entry rows in the sheet with next milestone and probability. Do you want the sheet updated in real-time or a weekly digest?
10:55 Oliver: weekly digest works for our ops team. We'll pick a day, Friday cadence preferred.
11:10 Sasha: Friday digest it is. I'll update the sheet and gate changes to the Friday snapshot.
11:28 Maya: quick question on pricing: do you offer partner discounts or co-sell rebate?
11:38 Sasha: Yes, there is a partner margin program for co-sell deals — specifics are in the partner playbook. Priya will follow up with the comp table.
11:50 Priya: will do, I'll add comp table to the shared drive.
12:05 Samir: technical blocker: for the retailer pilot they asked about GPU types and quantization. They use higher concurrencies during sales peaks.
12:20 Diego: we support multiple GPU types and can recommend quantization settings; for high concurrency we recommend continuous batching and autoscale policies. We'll propose configs.
12:40 Oliver: any legal/contract blockers? Procurement on their side will want data processing addendum.
12:52 Sasha: we have a DPA template, and we can add specific clauses for data residency and retention. I'll send it to your legal contact.
13:10 Maya: perfect.
13:25 Oliver: one more ask — for the healthcare deal they want a short timeline to get security sign-off; can you provide SOC2 and penetration test reports?
13:40 Sasha: yes SOC2 Type 2 and pen test summaries are in the security pack link I mentioned. If they need more detail we can arrange an NDA and provide redacted artifacts.
13:58 Samir: NDA will be needed for the pen test details. We'll get that process started.
14:10 Diego: noted. We'll prep the benchmark environment and request sample prompts and dataset.
14:25 Sasha: let's talk calendar — Diego proposed the tech deep dive week of 2026-11-15, any conflicts?
14:35 Oliver: fine for us. We prefer morning PST.
14:50 Priya: I'll coordinate and send invites.
15:02 Maya: on the pipeline, can we classify each opp by top obstacle? That helps focus enablement.
15:15 Sasha: sure — I'll add a column: obstacle (security, procurement, technical, pricing).
15:30 Oliver: good. For the fintech POC obstacle is procurement + audit logs. For health it's residency + KMS. For retailer it's pricing + concurrency.
15:48 Diego: technical note: for long-context clinical summarization we may need special kernel selection and larger KV cache; it may affect cost more than we'd like. We'll quantify.
16:05 Samir: also need to ensure model outputs match redaction requirements — PHI redaction is critical.
16:18 Sasha: we have structured output and redaction hooks — we'll demonstrate those in the deep dive.
16:33 Maya: any marketing support for co-branded case studies?
16:45 Priya: Redwood marketing can support a joint press release and a customer quote template — we'll run legal for approvals.
17:00 Oliver: timeline for that? Ideally early next year after first deployment.
17:12 Sasha: noted.
17:25 Diego: quick aside — competitors: customer asked about OpenAI's managed features. We should prepare a short battlecard.
17:40 Priya: I'll include a competitive battlecard in the enablement pack.
17:55 Oliver: Thanks.
18:10 Sasha: any other high-risk items we didn't cover?
18:20 Maya: RFP for government — need clarity on FedRAMP and procurement windows. We'll put that in priority 'early' because it's a long lead.
18:35 Samir: also integration points — they want audit log integration with Splunk. We can provide log export schema.
18:50 Diego: yes, we can map audit fields to Splunk/ELK, will provide schema.
19:05 Sasha: recap of next steps: I'll share updated pipeline spreadsheet by 2026-11-07; Priya will send enablement deck by 2026-11-10; Diego will schedule benchmarks and deep dive for week of 2026-11-15; Oliver will confirm top 3 opps by 2026-11-09.
19:30 Oliver: sounds good. Anything else?
19:40 Maya: no, thanks everyone.
19:46 Sasha: thanks all — we'll follow up in email and Slack channel, I'll drop the sheet now.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-attribution and filler words, some product names transcribed oddly (e.g., "Redwoods Dedicated"), timestamps are approximate.

End of transcript.
